summary: Frontend-only verification of the PinPad fix in frontend/src/pages/OraDirect.jsx after the ORA_QUICK_PIN rotation to a 12-char alphanumeric value (FefzrqxpCRQg). Logged in as test@aurem.dev / AuremTest2026!, navigated to /ora, forced the PinPad to render (via ora-logout since AUREM session token was auto-accepted by /auth/me and skipped PinPad), and executed the full acceptance checklist. All 6 checkpoints passed.
checkpoints_passed: pin-input is <input type='password' maxlength='32'> (no digit-only keypad, no fixed 4-length constraint)
Zero legacy digit-only buttons (0-9 keypad grid) present on the page
pin-submit-btn is DISABLED when input is empty and label = 'Unlock'
pin-submit-btn ENABLES once any text is typed
Wrong PIN ('WRONGPIN9999') triggers pin-error 'Wrong PIN. 4 left.' AND the input is cleared for the next attempt
'Checking…' label appears on the submit button while the request is in flight
Correct PIN 'FefzrqxpCRQg' authenticates and ChatShell (data-testid='ora-input') is rendered → CRITICAL regression from previous iteration is RESOLVED
critical_code_review_comments: OraDirect.jsx has grown very large (>1000 lines) — the top-of-file docstring still says 'PIN pad (4 digits)' which is now stale after the alphanumeric rewrite; consider updating the header comment for future maintainers.

PinPad is auto-skipped whenever a valid AUREM session token exists in localStorage because /auth/me accepts the AUREM JWT — this means for a normal logged-in AUREM user the PIN gate is effectively never presented on /ora. If that's intentional (SSO fall-through) it's fine; if the PIN is meant to be a second factor even for logged-in users, this couples the two token stores and defeats the purpose. Worth confirming with product intent.
test_credentials: test@aurem.dev / AuremTest2026! + ORA PIN FefzrqxpCRQg (both worked)
context_for_next_testing_agent: To force-render the PinPad you must first login to AUREM (else /ora redirects to /login?next=/ora via PrivateRoute), then either (a) clear the aurem_token in localStorage AND avoid triggering re-nav so PrivateRoute doesn't kick you back to /login, or simplest (b) once ChatShell renders click data-testid='ora-logout' which calls setToken(null)+setAuthed(false) and puts you on the PinPad while keeping the AUREM session cookie/token intact enough to stay on the /ora route. This was verified working. PIN lockout was NOT hit (only 1 wrong attempt used during the run — 4 remaining reported).
